item.title: Vacancy: Secretary
item.description: The European Union (EU) is an economic and political union of 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and cooperation with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic missions, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to that of an embassy. The EU Delegation to Australia, based in Canberra, works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. As a fully-fledged diplomatic mission, we represent the European Union in dealings with the Australian government in areas that o fall within the EU’s remit. JOB DESCRIPTION: SECRETARY (LOCAL AGENT GROUP 3) This is a one-year fixed-term post as Secretary within a team of four, with the possibility of a one-year renewal before potentially transitioning to a permanent contract, subject to budgetary availability and operational requirements. The successful candidate will be assigned responsibilities based on the evolving needs of the Delegation. They will work under the direct supervision of the Head of the Trade Section. Main Tasks and Duties: The following are the current key responsibilities: Provide administrative and logistical support to the Head of Section and the Trade Section team. Perform a range of administrative tasks, including: managing diaries, handling telephone enquiries, processing documentation, tracking events and activity registrations, responding to invitations. Draft, finalise, and dispatch notes, letters, and reports for filing and distribution. Arrange business trips, including all related administrative follow-up. Coordinate logistics for receptions, meetings, and conferences. Maintain and update contact distribution lists. Manage and review the Section’s electronic filing system. Additional Duties: Provide back-up for the secretariat of the Political, Press and Information Section, when required. Assist with back-up duties for the Ambassador’s secretariat. We are seeking an enthusiastic, highly motivated colleague to join our dynamic, results-driven team. Requirements: The ideal candidate should demonstrate the following: The ability to work both in a team and independently. The ability to prioritise tasks as set by the Head of Section and to organise work to meet deadlines with the highest level of accuracy. The ability to maintain strong professional relationships with all relevant stakeholders. The capacity to deliver high-quality work under time constraints. The ability to multitask effectively. A service-oriented and flexible approach. Remuneration and benefits: The base salary will be determined by verified, relevant employment experience and typically starts from AUD 6,740 per month (excluding superannuation). A competitive benefits package is offered, subject to certain conditions, and includes: personal leave entitlements, public holidays, and health insurance. Expected Start Date: mid-August 2026 Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered): Minimum year 12 certificate or equivalent Minimum of 2 years of experience in relevant fields (administrative and secretarial support, office organization etc.) Excellent knowledge (C2) of English Right to reside and work full-time in Australia (working holiday visa excluded) Assets/selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) Experience in a diplomatic mission or international organisation; Degree in the relevant fields (secretariat, administration); Proficiency in other European languages HOW TO APPLY The applicant must apply by sending: a cover letter ; a Curriculum Vitæ (to include, at the minimum, exact job titles, employers’ names and detailed tasks descriptions) using one of the Europass templates available at: https://europass.europa.eu/en if applicable: copy of the visa all documents to the following email address: Eeasjobs-132@eeas.europa.eu And mention in the email subject: “ [Name + Surname] – Application Secretary TRADE “ no later than 20/07/2026. Application Requirements: Your application must clearly demonstrate that you meet the four eligibility criteria listed above. This includes confirming that you hold full working rights in Australia. Only complete applications submitted on time via email will be considered. Selection Process Following the application deadline, eligible applications will be reviewed by the Selection Committee established for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, the selection process may include multiple stages, such as: shortlisting candidates based on an assessment of the information provided in their cover letter and CV, and conducting interviews. The three to five highest-ranking candidates will be invited to a final interview. Communication During the Process Only candidates progressing to each successive stage will be contacted individually. The Delegation will not provide additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During this time, candidates should refrain from contacting the Selection Committee members directly. Instead, any queries should be directed to the Delegation’s Administration team. The successful candidate will be required to undergo a medical examination and background check. Complaints Procedure Candidates wishing to raise a complaint about the recruitment process may submit a written request to the same functional mailbox used for their initial application. Upon receipt, the Delegation will review the matter and, if necessary, consult Headquarters before responding. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES The European Union is committed to an equal opportunities policy for all its employees and applicants for employment. As an employer, the EU is committed to promoting gender equality, preventing discrimination on any grounds and ensuring a zero tolerance approach to any form of harassment. It actively welcomes applications from all qualified candidates from diverse backgrounds. We aim at a service which is truly representative of society, where each staff member feels respected, is able to give their best and can develop their full potential. If pre-selected, candidates with disabilities are invited to contact the Delegation ( delegation-australia-hoa@eeas.europa.eu ) in order to accommodate any special needs and provide assistance to ensure equality of opportunities with other candidates. If a candidate with a disability is selected and recruited, the EEAS is committed to appropriate measures in order to accommodate his or her special needs to the working place or working conditions in accordance with Art 4 of the Decision ADMIN(2025)13 of the Director-General for Resource Management of the European External Action Service on providing reasonable accommodation for local staff with disabilities working in Union Delegations. item.description: The European Union Delegation to the State of Israel is looking for a Driver (male or female) We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through 145 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the State of Israel in Tel Aviv works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Israeli government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer A post of Driver (male or female) in the Delegation’s Administration Section. The contract (Local agent - Group V) will be concluded for an initial term of 2 years, with a possibility of extension, and will be subject to local legislation. The contract will foresee a probation period of 6 months. The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from ILS 8,253 up to a maximum of ILS 13,168. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of Section, providing technical and support assistance. We offer a competitive position in an international environment. The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience. There is a competitive benefits package, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurance and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be 15 September 2026. Main tasks Drive cars of the Delegation, strictly adhering to the Road code Provide safe transportation of Delegation staff or visitors in Tel Aviv and outside while on mission Daily monitor various EU Delegation cars - technical conditions, including checking on oil/ other fluids, tools, accessories and emergency equipment Ensure prompt service / maintenance / cleaning (interior and exterior) of the EU Delegation cars Immediately report to the Administration in the event of deficiencies, failures, damages or accidents Ensure timely and adequately filling of the petrol tanks Keep vehicle logbooks up to date Daily encode/update information on daily trips in the relevant IT applications Assist with Office and Delegation Expat staff cars registration / removal from registration Ensure compliance with the traffic rules - defensive driving style Run errands for the Delegation, mail deliveries, and light clerical works Any other task required in the interest of the service Compulsory requirements Medical fitness, excellent physical condition and good eyesight Minimum Secondary Education Valid driving license Minimum two years of professional working experience as a driver Knowledge of basic vehicle mechanics and routine vehicle care Spoken English – fluent Hebrew– fluent Assets Excellent knowledge of the local streets and traffic conditions and rules in Israel Successful completion of professional driver/security training C1 driving license (Armored vehicle) Experience with International Organization or Diplomatic Mission Knowledge of other European languages Basic IT skills Personal Skills How to apply Please send your application and supporting documents to eeasjobs-135@eeas.europa.eu The package should include a motivation letter, a detailed CV using the "europass" template ( https://europass.cedefop.europa.eu/ ) in pdf format. Incomplete applications will not be taken into consideration. The subject line of your application should indicate the post title: "Driver - Administration Section " Only complete applications in English received on time via indicated email will be considered. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure by telephone: please address any queries concerning this procedure to DELEGATION-ISRAEL-HR@eeas.europa.eu . If selected, the candidate will be required all supporting documents proving Israeli nationality/or permit of employment under local law, diplomas and professional experience declared in the CV. The process After the deadline for applications, the applications will be reviewed by a Selection Committee set up for this purpose. The Selection Committee will prepare a short-list of candidates who are considered the most suitable for the post based on a preliminary assessment of the information provided in their application letter and the supporting documents. The short-listed candidates will be invited to an assessment phase, which will consist of an interview. The candidates who have not been short-listed will not be contacted individually; however, the Delegation will use the same means of publication as for this Vacancy Notice to inform the remaining candidates once the recruitment procedure has been completed and that a candidate has (or has not) been recruited. The deadline for applications is 24 July 2026 at 13:00 (Tel Aviv time)

item.title: EEAS HQ - Assistant to the West Africa Division - AFRICA.3 - Contract Agent FGII - Job No 257278
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The AFRICA.3 Division is responsible for relations with the 16 countries in West Africa (Benin, Burkina Faso, Cabo Verde, Cote d’Ivoire, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone and Togo). The Division is also in charge of the relations with the Regional Economic Communities (RECs), being the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU), or other regional bodies. The Division is composed of 15 colleagues. Under the authority of the Head of Division, in the EEAS Managing Directorate for Africa and in close cooperation with the EU Delegations, the mission of the Division includes the following: Together with the EU Delegations, to shape the political relations with Western Africa countries, to promote and defend the essential principles of EU foreign policy, including human rights, democracy and good governance, and to contribute to development, peace, security and prosperity. To monitor political, economic and social developments and carry out analyses of the countries and the region. To support the HRVP in his work and to closely coordinate with the Council Working Party, PSC, FAC and other Council meetings on all questions relating to the political relations with the Western Africa countries and regional institutions. To support the implementation of wider EU policies on African and on global and cross cutting issues, including e.g. climate change, peace and security, trade and investments, democracy and human rights. To lead, in close cooperation with the European Commission, the multi-annual programming of development cooperation, in line with the relevant EU policies and objectives. To monitor and review country/regional development support strategies (annual, mid-term and end of term reviews); To ensure relations with the European Parliament and other EU institutions on Western Africa countries and the matters relevant for the region To contribute to the coherence of EU policies and instruments in the Western Africa region, including with other partners and institutions, civil society organisations and other stakeholders. To contribute to information and visibility of EEAS and EU policies and activities, including timely support to the spokesperson's office. WE PROPOSE The position of Secretary contract agent FGII as per article 3b of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (hereafter, the “CEOS”). Our recruitment policy is based on respect for diversity and on maintaining the gender balance. Our human resources management provides for balance between professional and private life, and support for training and developments opportunities. item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The RM.SCS.6, Real Estate, Safety and Greening Division is responsible for the definition and implementation of the Real Estate policy, Health and Safety as well as the Environmental Policies of the EEAS for HQ and the EU Delegations. In addition, it manages the buildings that host the EEAS in Brussels as well as the office buildings, official Residences and staff accommodations in 145 EU Delegations and Offices of the European Union worldwide. Background Erasmus+ is the European Union’s programme to support education, training, youth and sport. Erasmus+ also aims at boosting cooperation with Partner countries all over the world. The National Erasmus+ Offices (NEO) assist the European Commission, the EACEA, and the third country authorities concerned in the implementation of the Erasmus+ Programme. Their mandate covers supporting, promotion and dissemination activities related to the international dimension of Erasmus+ actions. For additional information on Erasmus+, please consult: http://ec.europa.eu/programmes/erasmus-plus/index_en.htm . He/She will be responsible for the implementation and coordination of the following activities: • Promotion, information and follow up of the Erasmus+ programme, including organisation of information campaigns, maintaining a website on upcoming calls for proposals, promotion material and activities, etc. • Support and training to local potential applicants interested to apply to Erasmus+, including organisation of training sessions and ad-hoc consultations on how to prepare a competitive proposal, as well as on specific topics of the EU programmes covered. • Dissemination and promotion of Erasmus+ project results, including communication and mainstreaming activities, as well as the provision of contributions to studies, statistics, reports and other analytical work for EACEA, the EU Delegation in Syria and national authorities in the fields of education, training, youth and sport. • Follow up of higher education issues and activities of the Erasmus+ Higher Education Reform Experts (HEREs), including the preparation of draft briefing papers and analytical notes, as well as reports on the implementation and progress of projects in which the higher education institutions in the country are involved. • Administration of the NEO, including managing the technical and administrative staff, monitoring the NEO budget and follow up financial issues, drafting NEO implementation reports. • Coordination , including cooperation and reporting on data, statistics and other relevant information to the EACEA, the EU Delegation and national authorities in Syria, establishing effective working relations with the other NEOs in the Erasmus+ Partner countries and the Erasmus+ National Agencies in the Programme countries. Experience in managing and coordinating a team. We develop and strengthen bilateral political, security, economic, cultural, educational, scientific and other sectoral cooperation between the European Union and Japan. Where relevant, cooperation with Japan also enables the EU to better promote and advance its interests and values at a regional and global level. The section is also responsible for organising public events, social media promotion and communication across all dimensions of EU-Japan relations. As an intern, you will get the opportunity to work within a dynamic, experienced, and international team of diplomats and policy experts. You will get a first-hand experience of political work in a diplomatic mission. You will gain analytical skills as well as practical opportunities to develop project management and organisational abilities. The busy EU-Japan calendar will offer opportunities to assist in the preparation and coordination of official and high-level visits as well as allow you to work on longer-term bilateral projects and events.
